units.essential_standard: Limits describe local and end behavior through graphical, numerical, and algebraic representations, and continuity connects those limits to function values and theorem-based conclusions.

mastery_goals.text: Determine and interpret one-sided, two-sided, and overall limits from graphical and numerical information, distinguishing limiting behavior from the function value.
Evaluate limits analytically by selecting and carrying out valid methods such as substitution, limit laws, factoring, conjugates, trigonometric limit reasoning, or squeeze reasoning when supported.
Analyze continuity at points and on intervals, including piecewise boundaries, by coordinating limits, function values, and discontinuity classifications.
Interpret infinite limits and end behavior and apply the Intermediate Value Theorem only when its hypotheses support the conclusion.

sections.title: What Is a Limit?
sections.learning_target: Relate average versus instantaneous change to the idea of a limit and read and interpret limit notation.
i_can: I can relate average versus instantaneous change to the idea of a limit and read and interpret limit notation.
I can estimate a limit from a graph or table.
I can connect shrinking secant intervals to instantaneous change.
misconceptions: Treating the function value at a point as automatically equal to the limit.
Reading a limit as a value reached rather than a value approached.
Confusing average rate of change with instantaneous rate of change.
modeling_applications: Estimate a limit from a graph or table.
Connect shrinking secant intervals to instantaneous change.
recurring_practices: Representation connection: Use the section’s graphical/numerical/symbolic representations to support the same mathematical conclusion and explain any apparent mismatch.
Interpretation: Connect the computed or inferred quantity to the variables/context and include units or sign meaning when the source situation provides them.
Notation / communication: Use the section’s limit, derivative, or integral notation precisely enough that the object, point/interval, and operation are unambiguous.

units.essential_standard: The derivative is a limit that measures instantaneous change and tangent slope, and derivative rules provide efficient ways to compute that change while preserving meaning, notation, and differentiability conditions.
